title: Where do the keyframes go when a clip has hard cuts?
fullTitle: FFmpeg libx264 -g 250 with Hard Cuts: -keyint_min 250 Gives 4 I Frames but 2 Keyframes

scenes.narration: You set dash g two fifty, and the clip has three hard cuts. Where do the keyframes go? Two, you would say: zero and two fifty. Four come out. Synthetic clip, f f m peg six point one point one.
captions: -g 250 on a clip with three hard cuts.
Two keyframes expected. Four came out.

scenes.narration: Three hundred frames, hard cuts at sixty, one thirty, two ten. Four readers of the same file: f f probe packets, the K flag; f f probe frames, the I type; Node reading the H two six four bytes; and x two six four's own count. A control clip has no cuts.

Defaults: keyframes at zero, sixty, one thirty, two ten. All four readers agree. Two fifty never comes: the last keyframe is at two ten, the next is due at four sixty, and the clip ends at two ninety nine.

Dash s c threshold zero, and dash x two six four params scenecut zero: the same file, every packet the same size. Keyframes at zero and two fifty. No keyframe at the cuts, one in the middle of a scene, and the file is nine percent bigger.
captions: Keyframes at 0 and 250, not at the cuts.

scenes.narration: Dash keyint min two fifty looks like the same switch. It is not. The cuts still become I frames: four. But only two are keyframes, zero and one thirty. Sixty and two ten are I frames with no K flag, and no N A L type five: three readers say so.
The rule: a cut becomes a keyframe only if it is far enough from the last one. Min keyint sixty: yes. Sixty one: no, and the count drops to three. Two fifty acts as one twenty six, the same file.
captions: Cut at 60: keyframe if min-keyint is 60.

scenes.narration: So dash g is a ceiling, not a schedule. Count K flags, not I frames. Not tested: other builds, other presets, B frames off, real footage.
captions: Not tested: other builds, presets, B frames off, real footage.
Count K flags, not I frames.
